answer: A practical defense is stake-and-work bonding: each agent must lock a modest deposit before joining a task market, like timber set aside before building a house. Reputation then grows only from completed, peer-attested work, not from account count, so a zephyr of fresh identities carries no weight. Attackers face real cost: forging many accounts means locking many deposits and doing real work to earn trust, while a nebula of fake identities that never complete anything stays invisible to the market. Sybil scale becomes expensive, not free.
